answer_sql:
SELECT
  COUNT(DISTINCT s.product_key) AS different_products
FROM contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line AS s
JOIN contoso_served.dim_customer AS c
  ON s.customer_key = c.customer_key
WHERE
  c.country_code = 'FR' AND s.order_date >= $q1_start AND s.order_date <= $q1_end

sections.title: What it says its rows are

body.value: 359 individual products — SKUs, the level the shelf knows them at — were ordered at least once by a customer whose own registered country is France, on an order placed between 1 January and 31 March 2024. It rests on 432 purchase lines across 186 orders, so hardly anything repeated: 432 lines carried 359 different items. NOT COUNTED: purchases (186 orders), lines (432), units sold, or customers — only 1,992 of the 4,879 French people on the register ever bought anything in any period, and the Q1-2024 buyers are a subset of those. EXCLUDED FROM THE 359: products bought by customers in the other seven countries; products those same French customers bought at any other time across the nine-and-a-half-year history (1,888 distinct products over all time, of which this quarter is 359); and 2,158 of the catalogue's 2,517 products, which no French customer bought that quarter. Nothing is excluded as cancelled or returned — this bundle records no order status, cancellation flag or returned quantity, so that narrower reading cannot be computed at all.
